title: Avoid Stepping into a Great Man's Shoes
coreMove: Step out of inherited comparison by creating a distinct center of gravity
sourcePressure: Chapter 41 centers on the danger of inheriting a powerful predecessor's place without creating a distinct identity. The law argues that succession fails when the successor lives inside comparison, imitation, or borrowed stature instead of establishing independent force. Its limit is that originality should not become performative rebellion or contempt for useful continuity. Frozen sidecar provides no traceable named anecdote for this chapter; do not fabricate named source anchors.
